claim: Miniature microscopes have gained considerable traction for in vivo calcium imaging in freely behaving animals.
source: Miniature microscopes have gained considerable traction for in vivo calcium imaging in freely behaving animals.
evidence: This is a general statement about the field that is presented as established knowledge in the abstract.

claim: Extracting calcium signals from raw videos is a computationally complex problem and remains a bottleneck for many researchers utilizing single-photon in vivo calcium imaging.
source: However, extracting calcium signals from raw videos is a computationally complex problem and remains a bottleneck for many researchers utilizing single-photon in vivo calcium imaging.
evidence: This claim is based on the authors' understanding of the field and the motivation for developing Minian.

claim: Most existing analysis packages have either key parameters that are hard-coded or insufficient step-by-step guidance and validations to help users choose the best parameters.
source: Despite the existence of many powerful analysis packages designed to detect and extract calcium dynamics, most have either key parameters that are hard-coded or insufficient step-by-step guidance and validations to help the users choose the best parameters.
evidence: This is a critical assessment of existing tools based on the authors' experience and serves as motivation for Minian.

claim: Large memory demand is often a constraint for setting up calcium imaging analysis pipelines since it limits the choice of hardware to specialized computers.
source: Moreover, large memory demand is often a constraint for setting up these pipelines since it limits the choice of hardware to specialized computers.
evidence: This claim is based on the authors' understanding of computational limitations in the field.

claim: Minian facilitates the transparency and accessibility of single-photon calcium imaging analysis.
source: Our open-source analysis pipeline, Minian (miniscope analysis), facilitates the transparency and accessibility of single-photon calcium imaging analysis, permitting users with little computational experience to extract the location of cells and their corresponding calcium traces and deconvolved neural activities.
evidence: This is a claim about the contribution of Minian, which is supported by the description of its features throughout the manuscript.

claim: Minian permits users with little computational experience to extract the location of cells and their corresponding calcium traces and deconvolved neural activities.
source: Our open-source analysis pipeline, Minian (miniscope analysis), facilitates the transparency and accessibility of single-photon calcium imaging analysis, permitting users with little computational experience to extract the location of cells and their corresponding calcium traces and deconvolved neural activities.
evidence: This claim is supported by the design features of Minian described throughout the manuscript.

claim: Minian contains interactive visualization tools for every step of the analysis.
source: Minian contains interactive visualization tools for every step of the analysis, as well as detailed documentation and tips on parameter exploration.
evidence: This is demonstrated through multiple figures showing interactive visualizations throughout the manuscript.

claim: Minian has relatively small memory demands and can be run on a laptop.
source: Furthermore, Minian has relatively small memory demands and can be run on a laptop, making it available to labs that do not have access to specialized computational hardware.
evidence: This claim is supported by the benchmarking data showing constant memory usage regardless of input data size.

claim: Minian has been validated to reliably and robustly extract calcium events across different brain regions and from different cell types.
source: Minian has been validated to reliably and robustly extract calcium events across different brain regions and from different cell types.
evidence: This claim is supported by the validation results presented in the Results section.

claim: The UCLA Miniscope project is a user-friendly miniature head-mounted microscope for in vivo calcium imaging in freely behaving animals that has been accessible to a large number of users.
source: The UCLA Miniscope project, a user-friendly miniature head-mounted microscope for in vivo calcium imaging in freely behaving animals, is one such project that has been accessible to a large number of users (Aharoni et al., 2019; Cai et al., 2016; Shuman et al., 2020; Aharoni and Hoogland, 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published work on the UCLA Miniscope.

claim: The principal component analysis or independent component analysis (PCA-ICA)-based approach was among the earliest algorithms that reliably detected the locations of neurons and extract their overall activities across pixels.
source: The principal component analysis or independent component analysis (PCA-ICA)-based approach (Mukamel et al., 2009) and region of interest (ROI)-based approach (Cai et al., 2016) were among the earliest algorithms that reliably detected the locations of neurons and extract their overall activities across pixels.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to the original publications.

claim: One of the limitations of PCA-ICA and ROI-based approaches is that activities from cells that are spatially overlapping cannot be demixed.
source: However, one of the limitations of these approaches is that activities from cells that are spatially overlapping cannot be demixed.
evidence: This is a known limitation of these methods cited from the literature.

claim: The CNMF algorithm was shown to reliably extract neuronal activity from both two-photon and single-photon calcium imaging data.
source: A subsequent constrained non-negative matrix factorization (CNMF) approach was shown to reliably extract neuronal activity from both two-photon and single-photon calcium imaging data (Pnevmatikakis et al., 2016), and demix the activities of overlapping cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to the original CNMF publication.

claim: The CNMF algorithm can demix the activities of overlapping cells.
source: A subsequent constrained non-negative matrix factorization (CNMF) approach was shown to reliably extract neuronal activity from both two-photon and single-photon calcium imaging data (Pnevmatikakis et al., 2016), and demix the activities of overlapping cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to the original CNMF publication.

claim: The CNMF algorithm models the video as a product of a 'spatial' matrix containing detected neuronal footprints and a 'temporal' matrix containing the temporal calcium traces of each detected cell.
source: The CNMF algorithm models the video as a product of a 'spatial' matrix containing detected neuronal footprints (locations of cells) and a 'temporal' matrix containing the temporal calcium traces of each detected cell.
evidence: This is a description of how the CNMF algorithm works, based on the cited literature.

claim: The CNMF algorithm is particularly effective at addressing crosstalk between neurons, which is of particular concern in single-photon imaging.
source: This approach is particularly effective at addressing crosstalk between neurons, which is of particular concern in single-photon imaging, where the fluorescence from overlapping or nearby cells contaminates each other.
evidence: This claim is based on the properties of the CNMF algorithm as described in the literature.

claim: By deconvolving calcium traces, the CNMF algorithm enables a closer exploration of the underlying activity of interest, action potentials.
source: Moreover, by deconvolving calcium traces, the CNMF algorithm enables a closer exploration of the underlying activity of interest, action potentials (Friedrich et al., 2017; Vogelstein et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to work on deconvolution methods.

claim: The original CNMF algorithm did not include an explicit model of the out-of-focus fluorescence that is often present in single-photon miniature microscope recordings.
source: Originally developed for two-photon data, the CNMF algorithm did not include an explicit model of the out-of-focus fluorescence that is often present in single-photon miniature microscope recordings.
evidence: This is a known limitation of the original CNMF algorithm as described in the literature.

claim: The CNMF-E algorithm uses a ring model as a background term to account for out-of-focus fluorescence.
source: This issue was addressed via the CNMF-E algorithm (Zhou et al., 2018), where a ring model is used as a background term to account for out-of-focus fluorescence.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to the CNMF-E publication.

claim: CaImAn is an open-source Python pipeline for calcium imaging analysis that includes both the CNMF and CNMF-E algorithms.
source: Later, an open-source Python pipeline for calcium imaging analysis, CaImAn, was published, which included both the CNMF and CNMF-E algorithms, as well as many other functionalities (Giovannucci et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to the CaImAn publication.

claim: MIN1PIPE uses a morphological operation to remove background fluorescence during preprocessing of the data.
source: The latest development in analysis pipelines for in vivo miniature microscope data is MIN1PIPE (Lu et al., 2018), where a morphological operation is used to remove background fluorescence during preprocessing of the data, and a seed-based approach is used for initialization of the CNMF algorithm.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to the MIN1PIPE publication.

claim: MIN1PIPE uses a seed-based approach for initialization of the CNMF algorithm.
source: The latest development in analysis pipelines for in vivo miniature microscope data is MIN1PIPE (Lu et al., 2018), where a morphological operation is used to remove background fluorescence during preprocessing of the data, and a seed-based approach is used for initialization of the CNMF algorithm.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to the MIN1PIPE publication.

claim: Most calcium imaging analysis algorithms have numerous free parameters that can influence the outcomes, without clear guidance on how these parameters should be set.
source: However, implementation of these tools can be complex as many algorithms have numerous free parameters (those that must be set by the user) that can influence the outcomes, without clear guidance on how these parameters should be set or to what extent they affect results.
evidence: This is a critical assessment of existing tools based on the authors' experience.

claim: There is a lack of ground-truth data for in vivo miniature microscope imaging, making it hard to validate algorithms and/or parameters.
source: Moreover, there is a lack of ground-truth data for in vivo miniature microscope imaging, making it hard to validate algorithms and/or parameters.
evidence: This is a known challenge in the field as acknowledged by the authors.

claim: Minian is based on the CNMF algorithm.
source: We based Minian on the CNMF algorithm (Giovannucci et al., 2019; Pnevmatikakis et al., 2016), but also leverage methods from other pipelines, including those originally published by Cai et al., 2016 and MIN1PIPE (Lu et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a direct statement about the algorithmic foundation of Minian.

claim: Minian leverages methods from pipelines originally published by Cai et al., 2016 and MIN1PIPE.
source: We based Minian on the CNMF algorithm (Giovannucci et al., 2019; Pnevmatikakis et al., 2016), but also leverage methods from other pipelines, including those originally published by Cai et al., 2016 and MIN1PIPE (Lu et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a direct statement about the methods incorporated into Minian.

claim: Minian implements an approach that supports parallel and out-of-core computation.
source: To enhance compatibility with different types of hardware, especially laptops or personal desktop computers, we implemented an approach that supports parallel and out-of-core computation (i.e., computation on data that are too large to fit a computer's memory).
evidence: This is a description of a technical feature of Minian.

claim: Minian has developed interactive visualizations for every step in the pipeline.
source: We then developed interactive visualizations for every step in Minian and integrated these steps into annotated Jupyter Notebooks as an interface for the pipeline.
evidence: This is demonstrated through multiple figures showing interactive visualizations.

claim: Minian integrates analysis steps into annotated Jupyter Notebooks as an interface for the pipeline.
source: We then developed interactive visualizations for every step in Minian and integrated these steps into annotated Jupyter Notebooks as an interface for the pipeline.
evidence: This is a description of how Minian is implemented and delivered to users.

claim: Minian includes detailed notes and discussions on how to adjust the parameters from within the notebook.
source: We have included detailed notes and discussions on how to adjust the parameters from within the notebook and have included all free parameters in the code for additional flexibility.
evidence: This is a description of the documentation provided with Minian.

claim: Minian includes all free parameters in the code for additional flexibility.
source: We have included detailed notes and discussions on how to adjust the parameters from within the notebook and have included all free parameters in the code for additional flexibility.
evidence: This is a description of a design feature of Minian.

claim: Minian comprises five major stages: preprocessing, motion correction, seed initialization, spatial update, and temporal update.
source: Minian comprises five major stages, as shown in Figure 1.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1 which illustrates the five stages of the pipeline.

claim: During preprocessing, the background caused by vignetting is corrected by subtracting a minimum projection of the movie across time.
source: During preprocessing, the background caused by vignetting (in which the central portion of the field of view is brighter) is corrected by subtracting a minimum projection of the movie across time.
evidence: This is a description of a specific preprocessing step in Minian.

claim: Sensor noise is corrected with a median filter during preprocessing.
source: Sensor noise, evident as granular specks, is then corrected with a median filter.
evidence: This is a description of a specific preprocessing step in Minian.

claim: Background fluorescence is corrected by the morphological process introduced in MIN1PIPE during preprocessing.
source: Finally, background fluorescence is corrected by the morphological process introduced in MIN1PIPE (Lu et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a description of a preprocessing step that cites the original method.

claim: Motion correction in Minian uses a standard template-matching algorithm based on cross-correlation between each frame and a reference frame.
source: The preprocessed video is then motion-corrected with a standard template-matching algorithm based on cross-correlation between each frame and a reference frame (Brunelli, 2009).
evidence: This is a description of the motion correction method with citation.

claim: The seed-based initialization procedure looks for local maxima in max projections of different subsets of frames and generates an over-complete set of seeds.
source: The seed-based initialization procedure looks for local maxima in max projections of different subsets of frames and then generates an over-complete set of seeds, which are candidate pixels for detected neurons.
evidence: This is a description of the seed initialization method in Minian.

claim: Seeds are refined based on various metrics, including the amplitude of temporal fluctuations and the signal-to-noise ratio of temporal signals.
source: Because this process is likely to produce many false positives, seeds are then further refined based on various metrics, including the amplitude of temporal fluctuations and the signal-to-noise ratio of temporal signals.
evidence: This is a description of the seed refinement process in Minian.

claim: The seeds are transformed into an initial estimation of cells' spatial footprints based on the correlation of neighboring pixels with each seed pixel.
source: The seeds are transformed into an initial estimation of cells' spatial footprints based on the correlation of neighboring pixels with each seed pixel, and the initial temporal traces are in turn estimated based on the weighted temporal signal of spatial footprints.
evidence: This is a description of how initial spatial footprints are generated in Minian.

claim: The CNMF algorithm first refines the spatial footprints of the cells (spatial update).
source: The CNMF algorithm first refines the spatial footprints of the cells (spatial update).
evidence: This is a description of the first step in the CNMF algorithm.

claim: The CNMF algorithm denoises the temporal traces of each cell while simultaneously deconvolving the calcium trace into estimated 'spikes' (temporal update).
source: The algorithm then denoises the temporal traces of each cell while simultaneously deconvolving the calcium trace into estimated 'spikes' (temporal update).
evidence: This is a description of the temporal update step in the CNMF algorithm.

claim: CNMF spatial and temporal updates are performed iteratively and can be repeated until a satisfactory result is reached through visual inspection.
source: CNMF spatial and temporal updates are performed iteratively and can be repeated until a satisfactory result is reached through visual inspection.
evidence: This is a description of how the CNMF algorithm is applied in Minian.

claim: Typically, two cycles of spatial followed by temporal updates are sufficient.
source: Typically, this takes two cycles of spatial, followed by temporal, updates.
evidence: This is based on the authors' experience using Minian.

claim: Minian includes a demo dataset that allows the user to run and test the pipeline immediately after installation.
source: Minian also includes a demo dataset that allows the user to run and test the pipeline comprised of the pre-made Jupyter Notebook immediately after installation.
evidence: This is a description of a feature included with Minian.

claim: The computation in Minian is optimized such that in most cases the memory demand for each process/core can be as low as 2 GB.
source: The computation in Minian is optimized such that in most cases the memory demand for each process/core can be as low as 2 GB.
evidence: This is a claim about the computational efficiency of Minian.

claim: The total memory usage of Minian roughly scales linearly with the number of parallel processes.
source: Regardless of the exact memory limit per process, the total memory usage of Minian roughly scales linearly with the number of parallel processes.
evidence: This is a claim about how memory usage scales in Minian.

claim: Minian currently supports .avi movies and .tif stacks.
source: Currently Minian supports .avi movies, the default output from the UCLA Miniscopes, and .tif stacks, the default output from Inscopix miniscopes.
evidence: This is a description of the file formats supported by Minian.

claim: Minian supports downsampling on any of the three video dimensions (height, width, and frames).
source: Minian supports downsampling on any of the three video dimensions (height, width, and frames).
evidence: This is a description of a feature of Minian.

claim: Two downsampling strategies are currently implemented in Minian: either subsetting data on a regular interval or calculating a mean for each interval.
source: Two downsampling strategies are currently implemented: either subsetting data on a regular interval or calculating a mean for each interval.
evidence: This is a description of the downsampling options in Minian.

claim: The vignetting effect in single-photon miniature microscope data can be easily extracted by taking the minimum fluorescence value across time for each pixel and subtracting this value from each frame, pixel-wise.
source: We find that the effect can be easily extracted by taking the minimum fluorescence value across time for each pixel and subtracting this value from each frame, pixel-wise.
evidence: This is a description of the method used for vignetting correction in Minian.

claim: Subtracting the minimum fluorescence value preserves the raw video's linear scale.
source: One of the additional benefits of subtracting the minimum is that it preserves the raw video's linear scale.
evidence: This is a claim about a property of the vignetting correction method.

claim: Minian uses a median filter by default to correct for salt-and-pepper noise on each frame.
source: By default, we pass each frame through a median filter, which is generally considered particularly effective at eliminating this type of noise, though other smoothing filters like Gaussian filters and anisotropic filters can also be implemented.
evidence: This is a description of the denoising method in Minian.

claim: A median filter is generally considered particularly effective at eliminating salt-and-pepper noise.
source: By default, we pass each frame through a median filter, which is generally considered particularly effective at eliminating this type of noise, though other smoothing filters like Gaussian filters and anisotropic filters can also be implemented.
evidence: This is a general statement about the effectiveness of median filters based on established knowledge.

claim: A window size that is too small for the median filter will make the filter ineffective at correcting outliers.
source: A window size that is too small will make the filter ineffective at correcting outliers, while a window size that is too large will remove finer gradient and edges that are much smaller than the window size, and can result in a failure to distinguish between adjacent cells.
evidence: This is guidance based on the properties of median filters.

claim: A window size that is too large for the median filter will remove finer gradient and edges and can result in a failure to distinguish between adjacent cells.
source: A window size that is too small will make the filter ineffective at correcting outliers, while a window size that is too large will remove finer gradient and edges that are much smaller than the window size, and can result in a failure to distinguish between adjacent cells.
evidence: This is guidance based on the properties of median filters.

claim: As a heuristic, the average cell radius in pixel units works well as a window size for the median filter.
source: As a heuristic, the average cell radius in pixel units works well since a window of the same size as an average cell is unlikely to blend different cells together, while still being able to adequately smooth the image.
evidence: This is practical guidance based on the authors' experience.

claim: Minian estimates the background using a morphological opening process first introduced for calcium imaging analysis in MIN1PIPE.
source: To accomplish this, we estimate the background using a morphological opening process first introduced for calcium imaging analysis in MIN1PIPE (Lu et al., 2018), which acts as a size filter that removes cell bodies.
evidence: This is a description of the background removal method with citation.

claim: The morphological opening is composed of two stages: erosion followed by dilation.
source: The morphological opening is composed of two stages: erosion followed by dilation.
evidence: This is a description of the morphological opening process.

claim: In morphological erosion, each pixel is substituted by the minimum value within the filter window.
source: In morphological erosion, the image is passed through a filter where each pixel will be substituted by the minimum value within the filter window.
evidence: This is a description of the erosion operation.

claim: The dilation process substitutes each pixel with the maximum value in the window.
source: Then, the dilation process accomplishes the reverse by substituting each pixel with the maximum value in the window, which 'dilates' small bright features to the extent of the filter window size.
evidence: This is a description of the dilation operation.

claim: The combined effect of erosion and dilation is that any bright 'feature' that is smaller than the filter window is removed from the image.
source: The combined effect of these two stages is that any bright 'feature' that is smaller than the filter window is removed from the image.
evidence: This is an explanation of how morphological opening works.

claim: Minian uses a standard template-matching algorithm based on cross-correlation to estimate and correct for translational shifts.
source: We use a standard template-matching algorithm based on cross-correlation to estimate and correct for translational shifts (Brunelli, 2009).
evidence: This is a description of the motion correction method with citation.

claim: In practice, the template-matching approach is sufficient to correct for motion artifacts that could have a significant impact on the final outcome.
source: In practice, we found that this approach is sufficient to correct for motion artifacts that could have a significant impact on the final outcome.
evidence: This is based on the authors' experience using Minian.

claim: Minian applies motion correction to the whole movie in a divide-and-conquer manner.
source: We apply this operation to the whole movie in a divide-and-conquer manner.
evidence: This is a description of how motion correction is implemented in Minian.

claim: Minian uses a seed-based approach introduced in MIN1PIPE to initialize spatial and temporal matrices for CNMF.
source: We use a seed-based approach introduced in MIN1PIPE (Lu et al., 2018) to initialize spatial and temporal matrices for CNMF.
evidence: This is a description of the initialization method with citation.

claim: The first step in seed initialization is to generate an over-complete set of seeds, representing the potential centroids of cells.
source: The first step is to generate an over-complete set of seeds, representing the potential centroids of cells.
evidence: This is a description of the seed generation process.

claim: Minian iteratively selects a subset of frames, computes a maximum projection for these frames, and finds the local maxima on the projections to generate seeds.
source: We iteratively select a subset of frames, compute a maximum projection for these frames, and find the local maxima on the projections.
evidence: This is a description of the seed generation algorithm.

claim: Minian takes the union of all local maxima across repetitions to obtain an over-complete set of seeds.
source: This workflow is repeated multiple times, and we take the union of all local maxima across repetitions to obtain an over-complete set of seeds.
evidence: This is a description of how seeds are aggregated.

claim: The iterative seed generation approach avoids missing cells that only fire in short periods of time that might be masked by taking a maximum projection across the whole video.
source: In this way, we avoid missing cells that only fire in short periods of time that might be masked by taking a maximum projection across the whole video.
evidence: This is an explanation of the rationale for the iterative approach.

claim: The spatial window for defining local maxima should intuitively be the expected diameter of cells.
source: During seed initialization, the first critical parameter is the spatial window for defining local maxima. Intuitively, this should be the expected diameter of cells.
evidence: This is guidance for parameter selection.

claim: A significant number of local maxima are usually false positives and do not actually reflect the location of cells.
source: Since the spatial window for local maxima is small relative to the field of view, a significant number of local maxima are usually false positives and do not actually reflect the location of cells.
evidence: This is an observation about the seed generation process.

claim: Thresholding the fluorescence intensity provides a simple way to filter out false local maxima.
source: Thresholding the fluorescence intensity provides a simple way to filter out false local maxima, and usually a very low value is enough to produce satisfactory results.
evidence: This is a description of a filtering strategy.

claim: A threshold value of 3 for fluorescence intensity usually works well for seed refinement.
source: We have found a value of 3 usually works well (recall that the range of fluorescence intensity is usually 0–255 for unsigned 8-bit data).
evidence: This is based on the authors' experience.

claim: Minian refines seeds by looking at the peak-to-noise ratio of the temporal traces and discards seeds with low peak-to-noise ratios.
source: Next, we refine the seeds by looking at what we call the peak-to-noise ratio of the temporal traces and discard seeds with low peak-to-noise ratios.
evidence: This is a description of a seed refinement step.

claim: Calcium dynamics are mainly composed of low-frequency fluctuations while noise is composed of higher frequency fluctuations.
source: Calcium dynamics are mainly composed of low-frequency fluctuations (from the slow kinetics of the calcium fluctuations) while noise is composed of higher frequency fluctuations.
evidence: This is based on the known properties of calcium imaging signals.

claim: Minian passes the fluorescence time trace of each seed through a low-pass and a high-pass filter to obtain the 'signal' and 'noise' of each seed.
source: Thus, to separate the noise from the calcium dynamics we pass the fluorescence time trace of each seed through a low-pass and a high-pass filter to obtain the 'signal' and 'noise' of each seed.
evidence: This is a description of the signal-noise separation method.

claim: The peak-to-noise ratio is computed as the ratio between the peak-to-peak values of 'signal' and 'noise'.
source: We then compute the difference between the maximum and minimum values (or peak-to-peak values) for both 'signal' and 'noise,' and the ratio between the two difference values defines the peak-to-noise ratio.
evidence: This is a description of how the peak-to-noise ratio is calculated.

claim: A cutoff frequency that is too low will leave true calcium dynamics absorbed in 'noise'.
source: A cutoff frequency that is too low will leave true calcium dynamics absorbed in 'noise' (Figure 9, left panel), while a frequency that is too high will let 'noise' bleed into 'signal' (Figure 9, right panel).
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 9.

claim: A cutoff frequency that is too high will let 'noise' bleed into 'signal'.
source: A cutoff frequency that is too low will leave true calcium dynamics absorbed in 'noise' (Figure 9, left panel), while a frequency that is too high will let 'noise' bleed into 'signal' (Figure 9, right panel).
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 9.

claim: A threshold of 1 for peak-to-noise ratio works well in most cases.
source: In practice, we have found a threshold of 1 works well in most cases.
evidence: This is based on the authors' experience.

claim: A peak-to-noise ratio threshold of 1 reflects the intuitive interpretation that fluctuations in a real 'signal' should be larger than fluctuations in 'noise'.
source: An additional advantage of using 1 is that it reflects the intuitive interpretation that fluctuations in a real 'signal' should be larger than fluctuations in 'noise.'
evidence: This is an explanation of the rationale for the threshold value.

claim: Minian refines seeds with a Kolmogorov–Smirnov test to check whether the fluctuation of values for each seed is non-normally distributed.
source: Finally, we refine the seeds with a Kolmogorov–Smirnov test. The Kolmogorov–Smirnov test assesses the equality of two distributions and can be used to check whether the fluctuation of values for each seed is non-normally distributed.
evidence: This is a description of a seed refinement step.

claim: Seeds corresponding to cells should be non-normally distributed.
source: We expect the noisy fluorescence values when a cell is not firing to form a Gaussian distribution with small mean value, and the fluorescence values when a cell is firing should have a much higher mean value and frequency than expected by the null Gaussian distribution. Therefore, seeds corresponding to cells should be non-normally distributed.
evidence: This is the rationale for using the Kolmogorov-Smirnov test.

claim: Minian uses a default significance threshold of 0.05 for the Kolmogorov-Smirnov test.
source: We use a default significance threshold of 0.05.
evidence: This is a description of a default parameter value.

claim: There will usually be multiple seeds for a single cell.
source: There will usually be multiple seeds for a single cell, and it is best to merge them whenever possible.
evidence: This is an observation about the seed generation process.

claim: Minian implements two criteria for merging seeds: the distance between the seeds must be below a given threshold, and the correlation coefficient of the temporal traces between seeds must be higher than a given threshold.
source: We implement two criteria for merging seeds: first, the distance between the seeds must be below a given threshold, and second, the correlation coefficient of the temporal traces between seeds must be higher than a given threshold.
evidence: This is a description of the seed merging criteria.

claim: The average radius of cells provides a good starting point for the distance threshold in seed merging.
source: While the distance threshold is arbitrary and should be explored, often the average radius of cells provides a good starting point.
evidence: This is guidance for parameter selection.

claim: A correlation threshold of 0.8 typically works well for seed merging.
source: The cutoff frequency should be the same as that used during the peak-to-noise ratio refinement described above, and the correlation should be relatively high (we typically use 0.8, but this can be refined by the user).
evidence: This is based on the authors' experience.

claim: Minian generates the spatial footprint for each cell by taking the cosine similarity between the temporal trace of a seed and the pixels surrounding that seed.
source: We assume each seed is the center of a potential cell, and we first calculate the spatial footprint for each cell by taking the cosine similarity between the temporal trace of a seed and the pixels surrounding that seed.
evidence: This is a description of how spatial footprints are initialized.

claim: Minian generates the temporal activities for each potential cell by taking the input video and weighting the contribution of each pixel to the cell's temporal trace by the spatial footprint of the cell.
source: Then, we generate the temporal activities for each potential cell by taking the input video and weighting the contribution of each pixel to the cell's temporal trace by the spatial footprint of the cell.
evidence: This is a description of how temporal traces are initialized.

claim: Minian estimates the spatial footprint of the background by taking the mean projection of the remainder after subtracting the matrix product of spatial and temporal matrices from the input data.
source: To estimate these terms, we subtract the matrix product of our spatial and temporal matrices, which represent cellular activities, from the input data. We take the mean projection of this remainder across time as an estimation of the spatial footprint of the background, and we take the mean fluorescence for each frame as the temporal trace of the background.
evidence: This is a description of how background terms are estimated.

claim: A cosine similarity threshold of 0.5 and higher works well in practice for initializing spatial footprints.
source: Cosine similarity is, in essence, a correlation (the scale is 0–1) and thresholds of 0.5 and higher work well in practice.
evidence: This is based on the authors' experience.

claim: A window size equal to the maximum expected cell diameter is reasonable for limiting the computation of pixel pair similarities.
source: In practice, a window size equal to the maximum expected cell diameter is reasonable.
evidence: This is guidance for parameter selection.

claim: CNMF requires that spatial noise over time for each pixel in the input video is first estimated.
source: CNMF requires that we first estimate the spatial noise over time for each pixel in the input video.
evidence: This is a description of a requirement for the CNMF algorithm.

claim: The spatial noise of each pixel is the power of the high-frequency signals in each pixel.
source: The spatial noise of each pixel is simply the power of the high-frequency signals in each pixel.
evidence: This is a description of how spatial noise is defined.

claim: The CNMF framework models the input video to be the product of the spatial and temporal matrices representing signals contributed by real cells, a background term, and random noise.
source: The CNMF framework models the input video to be the product of the spatial and temporal matrices representing signals contributed by real cells, a background term, and random noise.
evidence: This is a description of the CNMF model.

claim: Minian performs spatial updates for each pixel independently and in parallel to improve performance.
source: To reduce computational demand, we do this for each pixel independently and in parallel to improve performance, while retaining the 'demixing' power of the CNMF algorithm by updating the weights for all cells simultaneously.
evidence: This is a description of how Minian implements the spatial update.

claim: A sparseness penalty of 0.1 is considered appropriate for the example shown in Figure 11.
source: A sparseness penalty of 0.1 is considered appropriate in this case.
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 11.

claim: When the sparseness penalty is set much lower than 0.1, many additional 'fragments' begin to appear in the binarized spatial footprint.
source: When the sparseness penalty is set much lower, many of the additional 'fragments' begin to appear in the binarized spatial footprint, even if they are not part of the cell.
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 11.

claim: When the sparseness penalty is set too high, some cells are discarded during spatial update.
source: On the other hand, when the sparseness penalty is set too high, some cells are discarded.
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 11.

claim: The dilation window parameter determines the maximum distance a cell is allowed to grow during the spatial update compared to its previous spatial footprints.
source: Thus, the dilation window parameter determines the maximum distance a cell is allowed to grow during the update compared to its previous spatial footprints.
evidence: This is an explanation of the dilation window parameter.

claim: The expected cell diameter in pixels is a good starting point for the dilation window parameter.
source: The expected cell diameter in pixels is a good starting point.
evidence: This is guidance for parameter selection.

claim: During temporal update, Minian subtracts the background term from the input data and projects the data onto the spatial footprints of cells to obtain the temporal activity for each cell.
source: First, we subtract the background term from the input data, leaving only the noisy signal from cells. We then project the data onto the spatial footprints of cells, obtaining the temporal activity for each cell.
evidence: This is a description of the temporal update process.

claim: Minian estimates a contribution of temporal activity from neighboring overlapping cells using the spatial footprints of cells and subtracts it from the temporal activity of each cell.
source: Next, we estimate a contribution of temporal activity from neighboring overlapping cells using the spatial footprints of cells and subtract it from the temporal activity of each cell.
evidence: This is a description of the temporal update process.

claim: The CNMF algorithm models the relationship between the underlying 'spiking' and the calcium dynamics of a cell as an autoregressive (AR) process.
source: The CNMF algorithm models the relationship between the underlying 'spiking' and the calcium dynamics of a cell as an autoregressive (AR) process.
evidence: This is a description of the CNMF model.

claim: The 'spiking' signal in CNMF is modeled as a continuous variable rather than a binary variable.
source: It should be noted that although the underlying process that drives calcium influx is presumably cell firing, the 'spiking' signal is modeled as a continuous variable rather than a binary variable, and strictly speaking, it is only a deconvolved calcium signal.
evidence: This is a clarification about the nature of the 'spiking' signal.

claim: The exact relationship between the deconvolved 'spike signal' and the actual firing rate of cells is unclear.
source: It should be understood, however, that the exact relationship between this variable and the actual firing rate of cells is unclear since the absolute amount of fluorescence generated by a single spike, as well as the numerical effect of integrating multiple spikes on the resulting calcium signal, is unknown.
evidence: This is an acknowledgment of a limitation in interpreting the deconvolved signal.

claim: The coefficients of the AR model can be conveniently estimated from the autocorrelation of the estimated temporal activity.
source: The coefficients of the AR model can be conveniently estimated from the autocorrelation of the estimated temporal activity.
evidence: This is a description of how AR coefficients are estimated.

claim: In practice, it is helpful to first smooth the signal before estimating the AR model parameters, otherwise the time constant of the AR model tends to be biased by high-frequency noise.
source: In practice, we find that during the estimation of the AR model parameters it is helpful to first smooth the signal, otherwise the time constant of the AR model tends to be biased by high-frequency noise.
evidence: This is based on the authors' experience.

claim: It is computationally more efficient to break down the minimization problem in temporal update into smaller pieces and update subsets of cells independently and in parallel.
source: In practice, it is computationally more efficient to break down the minimization problem into smaller pieces and update subsets of cells independently and in parallel.
evidence: This is a description of the computational strategy in Minian.

claim: Minian identifies nonoverlapping cells using a Jaccard index, which measures the amount of overlap between the spatial footprints of different cells.
source: To do so, we first identify nonoverlapping cells using a Jaccard index, which measures the amount of overlap between the spatial footprints of different cells.
evidence: This is a description of how cells are grouped for parallel processing.

claim: During the temporal update, two additional terms are introduced: a baseline term to account for constitutive nonzero activity of cells and an initial calcium concentration to account for a 'spiking' that started just prior to recording.
source: During the updating process, two additional terms are introduced: a baseline term to account for constitutive nonzero activity of cells and an initial calcium concentration to account for a 'spiking' that started just prior to recording.
evidence: This is a description of additional terms in the temporal update model.

claim: Minian introduces a post-hoc scaling process to counteract the amplitude reduction effect of the ℓ1-norm.
source: To counteract this phenomenon, we introduce a post-hoc scaling process. After the temporal update, each cell is assigned a scaling factor to scale all the fitted signals to the appropriate values.
evidence: This is a description of a modification made in Minian.

claim: Users should choose an AR model order of 1 if near-instantaneous rise time is presented in the calcium dynamics of the input data.
source: Users should choose 1 if near-instantaneous rise time is presented in the calcium dynamics of the input data (i.e., from the relatively slow sampling rate) and should choose 2 otherwise.
evidence: This is guidance for parameter selection.

claim: A sparseness penalty of 0.008 is considered most appropriate for the example shown in Figure 13.
source: Here, a sparseness penalty of 0.008 is considered most appropriate.
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 13.

claim: A lower sparseness penalty will introduce many false-positive signals that do not correspond to real calcium dynamics.
source: A lower sparseness penalty will introduce many false-positive signals that do not correspond to real calcium dynamics, as can be seen in the plots.
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 13.

claim: Too high a sparseness penalty will produce false negatives where clear rises in the raw signal are not accompanied by spikes.
source: On the other hand, too high a sparseness penalty will produce false negatives where clear rises in the raw signal are not accompanied by spikes.
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 13.

claim: The CNMF algorithm can sometimes misclassify a single cell as multiple cells.
source: The CNMF algorithm can sometimes misclassify a single cell as multiple cells.
evidence: This is a known limitation of the CNMF algorithm.

claim: Minian implements a step to merge cells based on their proximity and temporal activity.
source: To counteract this phenomenon, we implement a step to merge cells based on their proximity and temporal activity.
evidence: This is a description of a post-processing step in Minian.

claim: All cells with spatial footprints sharing at least one pixel are considered candidates for merging.
source: All cells with spatial footprints sharing at least one pixel are considered candidates for merging, and the pairwise correlation of their temporal activity is computed.
evidence: This is a description of the cell merging criteria.

claim: Merging is done by taking the sum of the respective spatial footprints and the mean of all of the temporal traces for all cells to be merged.
source: Merging is done by taking the sum of the respective spatial footprints and the mean of all of the temporal traces for all cells to be merged.
evidence: This is a description of how cells are merged.

claim: Merging is only done between iterations of CNMF, but not at the end.
source: Since this is only a simple way to correct for the number of estimated cells and does not fit numerically with what the model CNMF assumes, merging is only done between iterations of CNMF, but not at the end.
evidence: This is a description of when cell merging is performed.

claim: Minian provides an interactive visualization to help users manually inspect the quality of putative cells and potentially merge or drop cells.
source: Minian provides an interactive visualization to help the users manually inspect the quality of putative cells and potentially merge or drop cells.
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 14.

claim: The result of manual curation is saved as an array with a label for each unit indicating whether a cell should be discarded or how several cells should be merged.
source: The result of manual curation is saved as an array with a label for each unit indicating whether a cell should be discarded or how several cells should be merged.
evidence: This is a description of how manual curation results are stored.

claim: Only the new label is saved during manual curation and no data is modified, allowing the user to repeat or correct the manual curation process if needed.
source: In this way, only the new label is saved and no data is modified, allowing the user to repeat or correct the manual curation process if needed.
evidence: This is a description of the non-destructive nature of manual curation.

claim: Minian can register cells across sessions using a simple approach based on centroid distances.
source: After completing the analysis of individual recording sessions, users can register cells across sessions. While more complex approaches are proposed in other pipelines (Giovannucci et al., 2019; Sheintuch et al., 2017), here, our intention is simplicity.
evidence: This is a description of the cross-registration approach in Minian.

claim: Minian aligns the field of view from each session based upon a summary frame to account for shifts in the field of view from one session to the next.
source: To account for shifts in the field of view from one session to the next, we first align the field of view from each session based upon a summary frame.
evidence: This is a description of the cross-registration process.

claim: A threshold of five pixels works well for the maximum pixel distance in cross-registration.
source: We found that a threshold of five pixels works well.
evidence: This is based on the authors' experience.

claim: A pair of cells must be the closest cells to each other in order to be considered the same cell across sessions.
source: Finally, a pair of cells must be the closest cells to each other in order to be considered the same cell across sessions.
evidence: This is a description of a criterion for cross-registration.

claim: Minian takes the union of all pairwise cross-registration results and transitively extends the cross-registration across more than two sessions.
source: We then take the union of all these pairwise results and transitively extend the cross-registration across more than two sessions.
evidence: This is a description of how cross-registration is extended to multiple sessions.

claim: Minian discards all matches that result in conflicts during cross-registration.
source: At the same time, we discard all matches that result in conflicts.
evidence: This is a description of how conflicts are handled in cross-registration.

claim: The cross-registration approach in Minian might be overly conservative.
source: We recognize that this approach might be overly conservative.
evidence: This is an acknowledgment by the authors of a potential limitation.

claim: The conservative cross-registration strategy provides an easy-to-interpret result that does not require users to make decisions about whether to accept cell pairs that could conflict across sessions.
source: However, we believe that this strategy provides an easy-to-interpret result that does not require users to make decisions about whether to accept cell pairs that could conflict across sessions.
evidence: This is the rationale for the conservative approach.

claim: Minian has been tested using OSX, Linux, and Windows operating systems.
source: Minian has been tested using OSX, Linux, and Windows operating systems.
evidence: This is a statement about the compatibility of Minian.

claim: The pipeline works on personal laptops for many common length (~30 min) miniature microscope experiments.
source: Additionally, although we routinely use Minian on specialized analysis computers, the pipeline works on personal laptops for many common length (~30 min) miniature microscope experiments.
evidence: This is based on the authors' testing of Minian.

claim: Any computer with at least 16 GB of memory will be capable of processing at least 20 min of recording data.
source: We anticipate that any computer with at least 16 GB of memory will be capable of processing at least 20 min of recording data, although increased memory and CPU power will speed up processing.
evidence: This is an estimate based on the authors' experience.

claim: It is recommended that the videos to be processed are held locally at the time of analysis, preferably on a solid-state drive.
source: Moreover, due to the read-write processes involved in out-of-core computation, we recommend that the videos to be processed are held locally at the time of analysis, preferably on a solid-state drive.
evidence: This is a recommendation based on computational considerations.

claim: The relatively slow speed of transfer via Ethernet cables, Wi-Fi, or USB cables to external drives will severely impair analysis times.
source: The relatively slow speed of transfer via Ethernet cables, Wi-Fi, or USB cables to external drives will severely impair analysis times.
evidence: This is based on the authors' understanding of data transfer speeds.

claim: Minian is built on top of project Jupyter.
source: Minian is built on top of project Jupyter (Kluyver et al., 2016) and depends heavily on packages provided by the open-source community, including NumPy (Harris et al., 2020), SciPy (Virtanen et al., 2020), xarray (Hoyer and Hamman, 2017), HoloViews (Rudiger et al., 2020), Bokeh (Bokeh Development Team, 2020), OpenCV (Bradski, 2020), and Dask (Dask Team, 2016).
evidence: This is a description of the software dependencies with citations.

claim: Both Minian and CaImAn achieve similar and near-perfect levels (>0.95) of F1 score across all simulated data conditions.
source: As shown in Figure 15, both Minian and CaImAn achieve similar and near-perfect levels (>0.95) of F1 score across all conditions.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 15 which presents the validation results on simulated data.

claim: The spatial footprints remain nearly perfect (>0.95) for both Minian and CaImAn across all simulated data conditions.
source: Similarly, the spatial footprints remain nearly perfect (>0.95) for both pipelines across all conditions.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 15.

claim: At the lowest signal level (0.2), both Minian and CaImAn suffer from decreased correlation of temporal dynamics.
source: At the lowest signal level (0.2), both pipelines suffer from decreased correlation of temporal dynamics.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 15.

claim: The decreased correlation of temporal dynamics at low signal level is likely due to noise and background contaminating the true signal.
source: This is likely due to noise and background contaminating the true signal.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the results by the authors.

claim: Minian and CaImAn pipelines perform similarly well in terms of output accuracy on simulated datasets.
source: Overall, these results show that the Minian and CaImAn pipelines perform similarly well in terms of output accuracy on simulated datasets.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the validation results.

claim: The deconvolved output from Minian is highly similar to ground-truth spikes when signal level is high.
source: Our results indicate that the deconvolved output from Minian is highly similar to ground-truth spikes when signal level is high, and the correlation asymptote and approach 1 when signal level is higher than 1.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 16A.

claim: The correlation between deconvolved signals and ground truth asymptotes and approaches 1 when signal level is higher than 1.
source: Our results indicate that the deconvolved output from Minian is highly similar to ground-truth spikes when signal level is high, and the correlation asymptote and approach 1 when signal level is higher than 1.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 16A.

claim: The lower correlation corresponding to low signal level is likely due to the background and noise contamination being stronger than signal.
source: The lower correlation corresponding to low signal level is likely due to the background and noise contamination being stronger than signal.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the results by the authors.

claim: The detected 'spikes' from the deconvolved signals closely match those from ground truth.
source: In line with this idea, the detected 'spikes' from the deconvolved signals closely match those from ground truth, as shown by the example traces in Figure 16B.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 16B.

claim: The main difference between deconvolved signals and ground truth is the amplitude of the deconvolved signals, which is prone to be influenced by local background and noise.
source: The main difference between the two traces is the amplitude of the deconvolved signals, which is prone to be influenced by local background and noise.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 16B and explained in the text.

claim: Minian can produce deconvolved signals that are faithful to ground truth and suitable for downstream analysis.
source: Overall, these results suggest that Minian can produce deconvolved signals that are faithful to ground truth and suitable for downstream analysis.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the validation results.

claim: Across six experimental datasets, the mean F1 score for matching ROIs between Minian and CaImAn is 0.73 (sem ± 0.03).
source: Across the six datasets, the mean F1 score is 0.73 (sem ± 0.03).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the experimental validation.

claim: The mean spatial footprints correlation between Minian and CaImAn on experimental datasets is 0.84 (sem ± 0.02).
source: The mean spatial footprints correlation is 0.84 (sem ± 0.02), and the mean temporal activity correlation is 0.86 (sem ± 0.02).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the experimental validation.

claim: The mean temporal activity correlation between Minian and CaImAn on experimental datasets is 0.86 (sem ± 0.02).
source: The mean spatial footprints correlation is 0.84 (sem ± 0.02), and the mean temporal activity correlation is 0.86 (sem ± 0.02).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the experimental validation.

claim: Most of the ROIs detected by Minian and CaImAn correspond to the same population of putative cells.
source: Our results indicate that most of the ROIs detected by Minian and CaImAn correspond to the same population of putative cells, and the resulting spatial footprints and temporal activity are nearly identical.

claim: The resulting spatial footprints and temporal activity from Minian and CaImAn are nearly identical.
source: Our results indicate that most of the ROIs detected by Minian and CaImAn correspond to the same population of putative cells, and the resulting spatial footprints and temporal activity are nearly identical.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 17.

claim: Cells detected by Minian and CaImAn tend to cluster near the center of the field of view, which usually has better signal-to-noise ratio.
source: These cells tend to cluster near the center of the field of view, which usually has better signal-to-noise ratio.
evidence: This is an observation from the experimental validation.

claim: Cells near the edge of the field of view usually have low intensity and spatial consistency due to the optical property of GRIN lens.
source: However, the cells near the edge of the field of view usually have low intensity and spatial consistency due to the optical property of GRIN lens.
evidence: This is based on knowledge of GRIN lens optics.

claim: Minian and CaImAn might detect different populations of cells near the border of field of view due to differences in preprocessing and initialization between the two pipelines.
source: As a consequence, Minian and CaImAn might detect different populations of cells near the border of field of view due to differences in preprocessing and initialization between the two pipelines.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the differences observed in the validation.

claim: The output of Minian is highly similar to CaImAn when analyzing experimental datasets.
source: Overall, these results suggest that the output of Minian is highly similar to CaImAn when analyzing experimental datasets.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the experimental validation.

claim: The run time of both Minian and CaImAn scales linearly as a function of input recording length.
source: As shown in Figure 18, the run time of both Minian and CaImAn scales linearly as a function of input recording length.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 18.

claim: The running time is similar across both Minian and CaImAn pipelines.
source: The exact running times vary depending on the number of cells as well as whether visualization is included in the processing, but in general the running time is similar across both pipelines.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 18.

claim: The peak memory usage of CaImAn scales linearly with recording length when the number of parallel processes was set to be constant.
source: On the other hand, the peak memory usage of CaImAn scales linearly with recording length when the number of parallel processes was set to be constant.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 18.

claim: The peak memory usage of Minian stays mostly constant across increasing number of frames.
source: At the same time, the peak memory usage of Minian stays mostly constant across increasing number of frames.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 18.

claim: The constant memory usage of Minian is likely due to the flexible chunking implementation where Minian was able to break down computations into chunks in both spatial and temporal dimensions.
source: This is likely due to the flexible chunking implementation of Minian (see 'Parallel and out-of-core computation with Dask'), where Minian was able to break down computations into chunks in both spatial and temporal dimensions depending on which way is more efficient.
evidence: This is an explanation of the memory usage pattern.

claim: CaImAn only splits data into different spatial chunks (patches), resulting in a linear scaling of memory usage with recording length for each chunk-wise computation.
source: In contrast, CaImAn only splits data into different spatial chunks (patches), resulting in a linear scaling of memory usage with recording length for each chunk-wise computation.
evidence: This is a description of how CaImAn handles data chunking.

claim: With more parallel processes the performance improves and the run time decreases but at the same time the total peak memory usage increases.
source: As expected, with more parallel processes the performance improves and the run time decreases but at the same time the total peak memory usage increases.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 19.

claim: In practice Minian is able to perform as fast as CaImAn, while maintaining near constant memory usage regardless of input data size.
source: In conclusion, these results show that in practice Minian is able to perform as fast as CaImAn, while maintaining near constant memory usage regardless of input data size.

claim: Minian allows users to process much longer recordings with limited RAM resources.
source: This allows the users to process much longer recordings with limited RAM resources.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the memory usage benchmarking.

claim: Place cells have been shown to have consistent place fields across at least 2 days.
source: Place cells have been shown to have consistent place fields across at least 2 days (Ziv et al., 2013; Thompson and Best, 1990) with only a minority of detected cells undergoing place field remapping.
evidence: This is a well-established finding in the literature with citations.

claim: On average, place cells have a correlation of ~0.6 for spatial firing rates across two sessions separated by 2 days.
source: We found that, on average, place cells have a correlation of ~0.6, which is consistent with the existing literature (Shuman et al., 2020).

claim: The average correlations between spatial firing patterns have higher values when the shifts are close to zero.
source: We found that the average correlations between spatial firing patterns have higher values when the shifts are close to zero (Figure 20B).

claim: Minian can reliably process in vivo calcium imaging data and produce results that are in agreement with the known properties of rodent CA1.
source: In conclusion, Minian can reliably process in vivo calcium imaging data and produce results that are in agreement with the known properties of rodent CA1.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the place cell validation.

claim: Ground-truth data for single-photon in vivo calcium imaging are lacking, making objective evaluation of the algorithms difficult.
